texts.facts: As the disputes in these writ petitions are the identical and are filed against the same respondents, these writ petitions are disposed of by this common judgment. 2. The petitioners in these writ petitions were the successful bidders in the tender floated by the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) for allotting of spaces within its bus station in Palakkad. Consequently, the petitioners erected temporary sheds within the above property on the Sureshkumar.T.R vs Palakkad Municipality on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186846451/ 4 strength of the No-objection certificate issued by the KSRTC. They had executed agreements and deposited the requisite amount with the KSRTC. Although the petitioners have submitted applications before the 2 nd respondent, to assign temporary building numbers for their WP(C) Nos.24796, 24658 & 29545 of 2023 2025:KER:50276 sheds, to enable them to apply for license, the applications have not been considered. Subsequently, they have also submitted representations to the 2nd respondent, to assign the temporary numbers. But, the representations have also not been considered till date. In W.P.(C) No. 20664 of 2023, a case of an identical nature, this Court had directed the 2nd respondent to consider applications for temporary building numbers. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the KSRTC submits that, the petitioners have already instituted civil suits before the jurisdictional Court and orders of temporary injunction have been passed against the KSRTC from evicting the petitioners from the property. Moreover, alleging that the temporary sheds have been unauthorisedly constructed in the property, the 2 nd respondent has refused to issue occupancy certificate to the KSRTC for their building.
